primary_antecedent.author: Lars Hörmander
primary_antecedent.title: The Analysis of Linear Partial Differential Operators III: Pseudo-Differential Operators
primary_antecedent.edition: Springer 2007, reprint of the corrected 1994 edition
primary_antecedent.locator: Theorem 18.1.35, printed pages 94–95; Theorem 24.2.1, printed pages 424–425; the parameter observation requirement in Section 24.7, printed pages 465–467.
primary_antecedent.receiving_contribution: Independent uniform reduction from an actual branch-strip norm to one fixed scalar interior observation, with a complete tangential-weight calculus and retained source/coarse remainders.

source_correspondence: M0 defines the joint symbol class with tangential weight and no bound on normal frequency, proves both Peetre inequalities and gives actual Schwartz and distribution actions.
M1 proves every finite composition remainder by an explicitly ordered integration-by-parts argument, then proves amplitude reduction, adjoints and proper-kernel errors in tangential order.
M2 proves all-real mixed mapping using the exact finite-derivative packet bound. Asymptotic summation simultaneously controls inverse symbols and their normal-frequency numerators.

M3 constructs the complete inverse away from one characteristic root, including arbitrarily high normal slopes. Right normal differentiation is exact; every lower term, nested-support error and proper-kernel derivative is retained.

M4 proves the actual interior strip estimate with one tangential derivative gained on the source and a retained coarse remainder. Normal input supports justify the cutoff equation without a new normal-source derivative.
O0 uses the complete current reflection factors and tests, a fixed positive strip and a common compact observed characteristic graph with a uniform support margin.
O1 decomposes the actual branch into the ordinary observed part and its complementary frequencies. Uniform graph separation and the coarse first normal jet control the full remainder.
O2 uses complete ordinary/tangential composition on bounded slopes, retains all ordinary smoothing tails and factors the observation family through one fixed scalar interior elliptic test.
O3 inserts the exact tested source equations into the earlier uniform reflection estimate. The two actual tangential source norms, full Dirichlet term and coarse mixed norm remain in the result.
O4 leaves the admissible source/Banach-domain conversion, global scalar assembly, other local uniform regimes and full parameter propagation open.
Three complete solutions verify the all-normal-frequency constant-coefficient inverse, the failure of tangential smoothing to improve normal regularity, and the exact reflected-mode boundary term.
Twenty-eight exact checks and 245 rendered formulas support the analytic review.
